summary: Hand-coded detectors flag style properties that perfectly separate labels in each sample (case, '!', bullets, greeting, sign-off, hashtag, gender, would/should closing). Corpus latents give linear F@g dependences: property coefficients by OLS on all 384 notes divided by a two-topic mean difference. A residual analysis on sample notes argues dependence ratios survive the SAE error. True logits on a few hand-built single-toggle notes (probes 0 and 2) calibrate borderline cues. Cues are kept when |dep| is large and its sign matches the label that carries the property. Latents are chosen greedily by per-latent gradient x property shift, under topic-retention floors computed from corpus and controlled minimal-pair directions; probe 2 splits 16 latents between two cues.

phases.purpose: Read task metadata, sample note structure and corpus examples; recognise a templated generator with independent style toggles.
Run ~23 regex detectors over samples; list properties perfectly label-correlated in each probe (confound set).
Extract activity/object phrases from corpus to build per-topic regex map.
Get per-probe gradients; compare F@g to SAE logits on 32 probe-0 sample notes (high correlation, offset).
Encode the whole corpus; univariate dependence = property F@g mean difference / topic F@g mean difference.
Logits and latents for all 128 sample notes per probe; study residual (logit - F@g) loading on within-label properties.
Check property independence in corpus; multivariate OLS; final dependence table with property coefs on all notes and topic coef on subset; rank suspects |dep|>0.12.
True logits on shared-baseline single-toggle notes for probes 0 and 2; compute local true/F@g ratio R and rescale corpus dependences.
Per-topic F@g spread shows corpus normaliser is typical; sign filter; scan extra surface features for missed confounds; fix cue sets.
Latent selection variants on corpus directions (ratio greedy, joint greedy, concentration curves, knapsack with topic budget).
70 controlled minimal-pair notes give clean topic/cue directions for probes 1 and 2; reselect latents under corpus and clean topic floors.
Per-cue greedy and split search for probe 2 with rho weights; probe 0 excl latents fixed; regex balanced-accuracy check on corpus; relaxed floors.
Inspect would_q latent concentration; finalise probe 1 via corpus-direction ranking with clean topic floor; scan probe-2 allocations.
Check ablation arithmetic: tool ablated-logit deltas vs F[:,S]@g[S] differ by a constant.
Rebalance gender vs would_q latents (2+14), assemble answer with structural checks, submit.

probe_query_use.purpose: true-logit dependences of excl/bullets/greeting relative to topic, and a true/F@g ratio to rescale corpus estimates

probe_query_use.text_kind: neutral fishing note, gardening counterpart, and fishing note with 'would you try it' closing
probe_query_use.purpose: true-logit dependence of the would-question closing and calibration ratio for probe 2

per_probe.procedure: Several style properties were label-perfect in the sample. Corpus OLS dependence ranked excl (-0.27), bullets (-0.22), would_q, greeting. True logits on single-toggle notes gave excl -0.23, bullets -0.16, greeting -0.06; ratios R rescaled corpus deps (excl -0.33, bullets -0.15, greeting -0.06). Greeting dropped by size and sign; excl kept as sole cue. Regex '!' (corpus balanced accuracy 1.0). Latents: corpus excl direction, ranked by gradient x property shift, added while corpus topic retention >=0.85 until removal reached 1.35x the F@g cue coefficient (16 latents).
per_probe.quote: - **probe0** (running/astronomy): main cue = **exclamation style** (dep ≈0.29–0.33, correct sign; error-term ρ≈2.07 confirms it's ≥0.15).

per_probe.procedure: Corpus dependence table showed hashtag +0.30 with every other property below ~0.07, so no true-logit text was spent. Regex '#'. Latent selection tried corpus and clean (minimal-pair) directions; removal plateaued near 56-59%. Final: rank by corpus hashtag direction benefit, accept a latent while clean-pair topic retention >=0.85 and corpus topic retention >=0.72, up to 16 latents.
per_probe.quote: main cue = **hashtag** (dep ≈0.30, 4–6× standout over all others)

per_probe.conclusion: gender (he/his/him) plus the 'would you try it' question closing
per_probe.procedure: Corpus dependence: gender +1.12, would_q +0.37. True logits on a would_q single-toggle triple gave +0.37 locally, rescaled estimate ~0.30, so both kept. Regexes for he/his/him and 'would you try it'. Clean minimal-pair directions showed latents nearly orthogonal to topic. Final split: candidates by corpus-direction benefit filtered to per-latent clean topic contribution <6%; scanned gender count 1-7 with rho-adjusted removal; chose 2 gender + 14 would_q latents by inspecting the table.
per_probe.quote: ng=2 maximizes the probability of solving probe2 (gender removal saturates at ~0.75 rmFg, would_q at 0.59).

per_probe.procedure: Corpus dependence table: largest properties excl +0.16 and bullets -0.14, everything else smaller. Judged below the cue threshold and inconsistent in sign with which label carries the property in the sample, so answered none without spending true-logit texts.
per_probe.quote: **none** — no property exceeds 0.16 and the sign-filter eliminates all candidates.

Corpus topic normaliser preferred over the single calibration pair after per-topic F@g spread showed the hand-built astronomy note was atypical.

caveats: The tool response formats in the API are assumed (arrays returned directly, probe_scores dict with logits/ablated). The cue decision for probes 0 and 3 (dropping bullets/greeting, excluding excl/bullets for probe 3) is encoded as an inspection constant since the sign filter was described but not coded. Several latent-selection variants are collapsed into abbreviated abandoned functions; their exact parameters varied across steps. The final probe-2 split (2 gender latents) overrode the scan's own max-min score, which favoured 1.
